# Incident Report: 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (AD domain: lafontainebleu.org, NetBIOS domain LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero |

Grounded via NBNS (`DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` name registration from 10.8.15.133), DHCP (hostname + MAC bound to that lease), ARP (MAC bound to 10.8.15.133), and Kerberos `CNameString` (`plucero`, `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$`) all from the same source IP.

## Malware Family
**Behavioral attribution: Latrodectus-style loader/downloader chain** (fake-invoice JS downloader → BITS-staged DLL → encrypted cookie-based HTTP C2). No IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory, so this is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed**.

Evidence for the chain (all timestamps relative to capture start):
1. **t=74.7s** - Edge 127 browser on the victim fetches `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (fake FedEx invoice-lure domain, Cloudflare-fronted at 104.21.55.70/172.67.170.159). The response body is a ZIP archive containing `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`.
2. **t=135.9-136.2s** - A `Microsoft BITS/7.8` job (User-Agent `Microsoft BITS/7.8`) issues HEAD then GET to `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — a bare-IP host with no domain, classic staging-server C2 tell. The downloaded object is a **PE32+ DLL** (`MZ` header confirmed), SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`.
3. **t=196.9s onward, continuing to the end of the capture (t≈1962s)** - Persistent HTTP beaconing from the victim to the same bare IP `72.5.43.29:80`: `GET /` and `POST /` requests carrying a large base64 blob in the `Cookie:` header and an obsolete spoofed User-Agent (`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`), with small binary/encrypted response bodies each time. This is the C2 check-in loop.

This sequence (fake shipping-invoice JS-in-ZIP lure → BITS-fetched DLL payload → IE6-UA cookie-encrypted C2 beacon to a bare IP) matches loader families in the IcedID/Latrodectus lineage seen in mid-2024 malvertising campaigns; naming it with certainty would require the payload's static/dynamic analysis or a signature match, neither of which is available here.

## Indicators of Compromise
